title: Chest X-ray: acute breathlessness
scenario: A synthetic adult presents with acute breathlessness, cough and reduced oxygen saturation. A frontal chest radiograph is available for an educational systematic-review demonstration.
clinical_question: Structure visible observations, assess technical adequacy and identify features that require urgent radiologist/clinician escalation.
systematic_review: Confirm projection/view, rotation, inspiration, penetration and coverage
Review airway and central tracheal position
Review lungs and pleural spaces zone by zone
Review cardiac silhouette and mediastinal contours
Review diaphragms and costophrenic angles
Review bones, soft tissues and visible upper abdomen
Check for devices, tubes, lines and prior-study availability
cannot_miss: Pneumothorax or tension features
Large pleural effusion or major collapse
Diffuse air-space pattern with clinical instability
Marked mediastinal abnormality
Critical device or line malposition
limitations: A single frontal view may not localise or exclude subtle disease
Portable AP technique can magnify the heart and mediastinum
Clinical findings and prior imaging remain necessary

title: Chest X-ray: tubes and line position
scenario: A synthetic post-procedure portable chest radiograph is being reviewed for the position of visible support devices and immediate complications.
clinical_question: Describe visible devices without inventing type or course, and flag any potentially critical malposition or post-procedure complication for immediate human review.
systematic_review: Identify every visible tube, line, drain, wire or device
Trace each visible device along its complete imaged course
State whether the tip is visible and where it projects
Check lungs and pleura for post-procedure complications
Check mediastinum, cardiac silhouette and diaphragms
Compare with prior or procedural documentation when available
cannot_miss: Possible endotracheal, enteric or central line malposition
New pneumothorax
New large pleural collection or collapse
Device fragmentation or unexpected course
limitations: Projection does not prove intravascular or intraluminal location
Device identity and intended target must be confirmed from documentation
Immediate escalation follows local protocol

title: Non-contrast CT head: acute neurological symptoms
scenario: A synthetic patient has sudden focal neurological symptoms. Selected non-contrast CT head images are available for a teaching demonstration.
clinical_question: Use a systematic acute CT head checklist and explicitly state that selected screenshots cannot replace review of the full series.
systematic_review: Confirm study type, coverage, reconstruction and artefact
Review for acute haemorrhage by compartment
Assess grey-white differentiation and focal hypoattenuation
Assess mass effect, sulci, ventricles, cisterns and midline
Review posterior fossa on the complete series
Review calvarium, skull base, sinuses and mastoids
Confirm whether angiographic/perfusion imaging exists
cannot_miss: Acute intracranial haemorrhage
Mass effect, herniation or hydrocephalus
Large-territory early ischaemic change
Acute fracture with intracranial complication
limitations: A screenshot or one slice cannot exclude acute pathology
Windowing and complete multiplanar review are required
Stroke decisions require the authorised acute-stroke workflow

title: CT pulmonary angiography: suspected embolism
scenario: A synthetic CT pulmonary angiography case is used to demonstrate how AI should first assess contrast timing, motion and study completeness before describing possible filling defects.
clinical_question: Structure technical adequacy, vascular observations and urgent associated findings without declaring or excluding embolism from selected images.
systematic_review: Confirm angiographic phase, pulmonary arterial enhancement and motion
Review central through segmental pulmonary arteries on the full series
Check right-heart and septal appearance without inventing measurements
Review lung parenchyma, pleura and airways
Review mediastinum, aorta, upper abdomen and bones
Check for alternative or associated urgent findings
cannot_miss: Central or extensive pulmonary arterial filling defect
Possible right-heart strain features
Aortic emergency visible in the imaged field
Pneumothorax or other immediate thoracic emergency
limitations: Selected images cannot exclude segmental or subsegmental emboli
Poor contrast timing or motion may make the study non-diagnostic
Clinical probability and authorised management pathway remain essential

title: MRI brain: mass or treatment follow-up
scenario: A synthetic MRI brain follow-up case includes selected sequences from a patient with a previously documented intracranial lesion.
clinical_question: Describe sequence-specific observations and comparison needs without assigning tumour type, progression or treatment response from incomplete images.
systematic_review: List available and missing sequences, planes and contrast status
Review lesion location, signal, margins and mass effect
Review enhancement only if pre/post-contrast images are available
Review diffusion and susceptibility when available
Review oedema, ventricles, cisterns and midline
Review remaining brain, extra-axial spaces and visible skull base
State the need for comparison with prior MRI
cannot_miss: Marked mass effect or herniation features
Acute haemorrhage or restricted diffusion
Obstructive hydrocephalus
Unexpected acute treatment complication
limitations: Do not infer enhancement without matched pre/post-contrast sequences
Do not assign tumour grade, molecular type or progression
Formal response assessment requires protocol-compliant complete studies and priors

title: MRI spine: pain with neurological red flags
scenario: A synthetic patient has back pain and neurological red flags. Selected MRI spine images are available for educational review.
clinical_question: Structure level-by-level observations and identify features requiring urgent escalation while acknowledging incomplete coverage.
systematic_review: Confirm spinal region, sequences, planes and coverage
Review alignment, vertebral bodies and marrow signal
Review discs, canal, lateral recesses and neural foramina
Review spinal cord/conus/cauda equina as applicable
Review paraspinal and prevertebral soft tissues
Localise observations by the documented vertebral numbering method
Check prior imaging and clinical neurological level
cannot_miss: Severe canal compromise with neural compression
Cord/conus signal abnormality
Possible infection, epidural collection or destructive lesion
Acute unstable injury features
limitations: Do not invent vertebral numbering when transitional anatomy is possible
Selected sequences cannot exclude subtle cord, marrow or soft-tissue disease
Urgent neurological findings require direct clinical escalation

title: Musculoskeletal X-ray: acute trauma
scenario: A synthetic trauma case includes radiographs of an injured extremity for a systematic alignment, bone, joint and soft-tissue review.
clinical_question: Describe visible traumatic findings and image adequacy without assigning management or clearing the injury from inadequate views.
systematic_review: Confirm patient side marker, projections and inclusion of relevant joints
Review alignment and cortical continuity
Review trabecular pattern and focal bone density
Review joint congruity and joint spaces
Review soft-tissue swelling, gas and foreign material
Check for additional injuries within the field
State whether orthogonal or special views are missing
cannot_miss: Displaced or open-injury-associated fracture pattern
Joint dislocation or major incongruity
Neurovascular-risk alignment abnormality
Soft-tissue gas or unexpected foreign body
limitations: One projection cannot reliably exclude fracture or dislocation
Age-specific ossification and subtle injuries require expert review
Clinical tenderness and neurovascular examination remain essential

title: Abdominal ultrasound: right upper-quadrant pain
scenario: A synthetic patient has right upper-quadrant pain. Selected ultrasound still images are available without the complete dynamic examination.
clinical_question: Structure visible observations, missing views and required measurements without declaring a diagnosis from selected still images.
systematic_review: Confirm organs/views represented and technical limitations
Review gallbladder lumen, wall and surrounding region
Review visible biliary tree and documented measurements
Review liver echotexture and focal observations
Review visible portal/hepatic vessels when provided
Review right kidney and visible adjacent structures
State which dynamic manoeuvres and Doppler views are absent
cannot_miss: Marked biliary dilatation or obstructive pattern
Pericholecystic collection or other complication feature
Large focal abnormality requiring urgent review
Unexpected free fluid in an unstable patient
limitations: Ultrasound is operator- and acquisition-dependent
Still images cannot reproduce probe compression, tenderness or dynamic scanning
Measurements and Doppler settings must not be invented

title: Obstetric ultrasound: structured review
scenario: A synthetic obstetric ultrasound teaching case contains selected de-identified still images and documented measurements.
clinical_question: Organise the supplied observations and missing elements without estimating unprovided measurements, gestational conclusions or fetal status.
systematic_review: Confirm stated indication, gestational context and study scope
List available views and documented measurements exactly
Review documented fetal number, presentation and cardiac activity only when shown
Review placenta, fluid and cervix only when adequately represented
Review anatomy according to the stated examination type
List all required views or measurements that are absent
Confirm comparison and follow-up ownership
cannot_miss: Any documented absence/abnormality of cardiac activity requiring immediate professional review
Major placental or bleeding-related concern
Severe fluid abnormality or other urgent documented feature
Maternal emergency visible or described in the supplied context
limitations: Do not infer fetal well-being from selected images
Do not invent gestational age, growth percentile or biometric measurements
Do not make sex determination or disclose protected information
Local legal and professional requirements apply

title: Mammography: screening or diagnostic review
scenario: A synthetic mammography case includes selected standard views for an educational comparison and reporting-structure demonstration.
clinical_question: Structure observations, comparison requirements and limitations without assigning a final BI-RADS category or screening disposition.
systematic_review: Confirm exam type, laterality, standard views and image adequacy
Review breast composition only when professionally assessable
Compare sides and available prior studies
Review for masses, asymmetries, distortion and calcifications
Review skin, nipple, axillary regions and visible nodes
Localise observations by side, view and depth without inventing measurements
State whether targeted ultrasound or additional views are already available
cannot_miss: Suspicious mass, distortion or calcification pattern
Concerning interval change from prior imaging
Skin/nipple change requiring prompt correlation
Technically inadequate study needing professional recall decision
limitations: Selected or compressed screenshots are inadequate for screening interpretation
Prior comparison and full-resolution approved workstations are required
Do not assign final BI-RADS, malignancy probability or patient disposition
